senses.gloss: f. (סרר, cmp. אסטרניא, אצטרניא P. Sm. 304 a. quot. ibid.; cmp. אֲבֵידָן) place of debauchery, an opprobrious name for the theatres, arenas &c. of the Romans, and a phonetic perversion of theatrum, θέατρον.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 1:7">Ab. Zar. I, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 16a">16ᵃ</cite>) you must not build … <he>גרדום אצטדייא וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>אצטריבא</he>, prob. <he>אצטרינא</he>, v. supra; in Ib. 18ᵇ repeatedly <he>אצטר׳</he>, Mishn. Nap. <cite ref="A02865"><he>אצטדיא</he></cite>, in comment. ib. <he>אצטרדיא</he>), expl. ib. 16ᵇ <he>בסיליקי של גרדום וכ׳</he> a building for public execution (court) or for public entertainment (amphitheatre &c.)—Pl. <cite ref="A02350"><he>אִסְטַרְיוֹת</he></cite>. Sifra Aḥare IX, 13. [<cite ref="Menachot 103b:20">Men. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>איסטריא של מלך</he> royal amphitheatre(?), v. <cite ref="A02412"><he>אסטרטיא</he></cite>.] [Tanḥ.
B’resh. 2 אִסְטְרָטָאוֹת, Var. אִסְטְרָאוֹת theatres.] Ab. Zar. 18ᵇ לא הלך לאיסטרטאות Ms. M. (ed. טַרְטְיָאוֹת q. v.; En Yak. תרט׳). [For the vers. אִצְטַדְיָא v. s. v.]
